rows.source: HSE diving at work
rows.verified: Diving at work is a high-hazard activity controlled by the Diving at Work Regulations 1997.

rows.source: HSE diving at work
rows.verified: The regulations cover diving projects where one or more divers are at work, whether employed or self-employed.

rows.source: HSE diving at work
rows.verified: Duties extend across the diving project, from the client commissioning the work to the diver carrying it out.

rows.source: HSE diving at work
rows.verified: Working divers must hold an HSE-approved qualification relevant and sufficient for the class of diving work.

rows.source: HSE diving at work
rows.verified: Divers must be competent to work safely as well as having the technical skills needed for the underlying job.

rows.source: HSE diving at work
rows.verified: Divers at work must hold a valid certificate of medical fitness issued following examination by an HSE-approved medical examiner of divers.

rows.source: HSE diving at work
rows.verified: HSE recognises commercial competence standards for SCUBA, surface-supplied, surface-supplied top-up and closed-bell diving.

rows.source: HSE diving at work
rows.verified: A certificate of medical fitness to dive is valid for up to 12 months and must be renewed through an annual medical examination.

rows.source: HSE diving at work
rows.verified: Diving controls depend on the diving class, depth, breathing system, work task, environment, team competence, medical fitness and emergency arrangements.

rows.source: HSE diving at work
rows.verified: Diving guidance is project-, diver-, equipment-, task- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury or fatality probability.

rows.source: HSE offshore fire, explosion and emergency response
rows.verified: HSE's L65 ACOP provides practical guidance for complying with the Offshore Installations (Prevention of Fire and Explosion, and Emergency Response) Regulations 1995.

rows.source: HSE offshore fire, explosion and emergency response
rows.verified: The guidance addresses prevention of offshore fires and explosions and protection of people if such events occur.

rows.source: HSE offshore fire, explosion and emergency response
rows.verified: Emergency-response planning must consider escape, evacuation, rescue and recovery.

rows.source: HSE offshore fire, explosion and emergency response
rows.verified: Fire and explosion hazard management should provide for timely detection and appropriate reporting and recording of events.

rows.source: HSE offshore fire, explosion and emergency response
rows.verified: Assessments must consider toxic or asphyxiating gas releases that could require evacuation, escape or rescue.

rows.source: HSE offshore fire, explosion and emergency response
rows.verified: Detection arrangements should address suitable systems, alarm settings and the capabilities needed for the hazard.

rows.source: HSE offshore fire, explosion and emergency response
rows.verified: Emergency plans should define temporary-refuge survival time and address events that could compromise refuge integrity.

rows.source: HSE offshore fire, explosion and emergency response
rows.verified: PFEER includes duties concerning emergency-response initiation, liaison with external responders and early warning of major accidents.

rows.source: HSE offshore fire, explosion and emergency response
rows.verified: Offshore emergency controls depend on hydrocarbon inventory, ignition potential, detection coverage, containment, installation layout, weather, occupancy and evacuation resources.

rows.source: HSE offshore fire, explosion and emergency response
rows.verified: Offshore PFEER evidence is installation-, scenario-, barrier- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level major-accident probability.
